submissionAttempts.body:
Conclusion: When a stored observation (state change-feed) cursor is rejected, the integration must expect Ordarium's `InvalidCursorError`, whose stable string code is `"INVALID_CURSOR"`. It should NOT expect the historical numeric code 27.

Evidence and decision:
1. Governing source = the exact pinned dependency contract. `package.json` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (overrides) pin all four `@ordarium/*` packages to release ordarium-v1.3.1, and the installed artifact matches (`node_modules/@ordarium/core/package.json` = 1.3.1). In `node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/errors.js` (and errors.d.ts) `InvalidCursorError` is declared with `super("INVALID_CURSOR", "The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point")`. It is part of the public surface (`index.d.ts` re-exports errors.js).
2. Where it fires: the state change feed is the observation surface — `state.d.ts`/`types.d.ts` document `changes(filter?, cursor?)` as "Incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position (ORD-BOOT-0)", returning an always-present opaque durable `cursor`. `ledger-sqlite`'s (and `MemoryLedger`'s) `changes()` throw `InvalidCursorError` when the caller-supplied cursor cannot be decoded as the opaque base64url `{"c":"<digits>"}` position, or when it is syntactically valid but exceeds the ledger's global commit high-water mark (foreign/restored/replaced ledger). `createStateStore().changes()` delegates to the ledger and protects only the capability gate, so this error surfaces unchanged to a consumer.
3. Failure characteristics: it is a caller-input failure that fails closed (no silent restart from the beginning of the feed). It is deliberately distinct from `LEDGER_CORRUPT` (damaged ledger content) and from `LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED` (feed capability absent), and it is not a transient/busy retry condition.
4. Why not 27: the only source for "27" is `docs/engineering/notes/error-code-note.md`, which declares itself "informational, not normative". Per `docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md`, the published contract of the exact pinned version governs that dependency interface, and informational records "never override 1 or 2" (here the pinned contract). Independent corroboration that 27 is unreliable: `docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md` assigns numeric codes 27–29 to STATE_REVISION_CONFLICT / STATE_REF_NOT_FOUND and its §3.2 item 4 mandates mapping Ordarium errors by `instanceof` into the classification system rather than hardcoding numeric codes. The note is also stale relative to the pin (docs describe a 1.2.0 baseline; the pin and install are 1.3.1).

Integration rule: catch/inspect by identity — `error instanceof InvalidCursorError` (or `error.code === "INVALID_CURSOR"`) — and treat it as a fail-closed, non-retryable input error, not as ledger corruption and not as a retryable busy/transient condition.

No peer contact was needed: the pinned v1.3.1 artifact shipped in this workspace is the authoritative contract for the dependency interface, so local source-precedence analysis fully decides the question.
